extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems with full step-by-step solutions. It is designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability in machine learning models across multiple subjects and difficulty levels.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMPS consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code. MATH problems are created by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MATH competition problems from the Mathematical Association of America (MAA); AMPS problems generated from Khan Academy modules using Mathematica and Khan Academy code.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each MATH problem has a full step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer; the paper says these solutions are used to train models to generate answer derivations and explanations. It also states that problems and solutions are consistently formatted using LaTeX and Asymptote, and that the final answers follow consistent formatting rules for exact-match evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper evaluates answer quality via automatic exact-match scoring using boxed answers and formatting normalization, and it also reports human-level performance on a random sample of 20 test problems. It further analyzes model confidence with AUROC for detecting correct vs. incorrect answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: All human evaluators mentioned were university students; specific examples include a computer science PhD student, a participant who does not like mathematics, participants who like mathematics, a participant who scored perfectly on AMC 10 and attended USAMO several times, and a three-time IMO gold medalist.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is biased toward high school competition mathematics from U.S. contests and specific subjects/difficulty levels; the paper also notes that the problems are from competitions that "assess the mathematical problem-solving ability of the best young mathematical talent in the United States."
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging and current models achieve low accuracy; the paper says scaling alone is unlikely to solve it and that future progress will require algorithmic advances. It also notes that generated step-by-step solutions can be wrong or misleading, and that even with 99% of a solution visible models still struggle.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper suggests potential educational implications and warns about cheating on homework if models become strong at the task. It also frames solving MATH as having "profound practical and intellectual significance."
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking/testing mathematical problem-solving ability, and the step-by-step solutions can be used for training/fine-tuning models to generate derivations and explanations. The paper also describes training on MATH and pretraining on AMPS.
